description_full: Sea Limited, through its subsidiaries, operates as a technology company in Southeast Asia, Latin America, the rest of Asia, and internationally. The company operates through E-commerce, Digital Financial Services, and Digital Entertainment segments. It offers Garena, a digital entertainment platform for users to access mobile and PC online games, as well as promotes eSports operations and develops games. The company also operates the Shopee e-commerce platform, a mobile-centric marketplace that provides integrated payments, logistics and fulfillment infrastructure, and other value-added services. In addition, it offers Monee digital financial services comprising consumer, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) credit, e- wallets, payment processing, banking, Insurtech, and wealth services; and acts as an underwriter for various life and non-life insurance products under the MoneeInsure tradename, as well as insurance agency services. It serves buyers, such as individuals and households; and sellers, including small and medium businesses, brands, and large retailers. The company was formerly known as Garena Interactive Holding Limited and changed its name to Sea Limited in April 2017. Sea Limited was incorporated in 2009 and is headquartered in Singapore.

financial_summary: Sea Limited is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $46.4B market cap on $22.9B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +23% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +16.2pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 41% against a 11% cost of capital — a 29-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 39%.

The business throws off $4.5B in free cash flow — roughly 20 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.18× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -11.7% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 59× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 0.1% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 26% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 9% operating margin is roughly in line with the Consumer Cyclical median (8%).
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.05x).
It accounts for 0.4% of sector revenue and 0.5% of sector operating profit.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 377 companies in the universe; the top four hold 26% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 37% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 52% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 51% and a beta of 1.35, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 2.06 vs 5y 1.73), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $482.8M traded a day, and interest is running hot at 1.5x its yearly average volume.
In past sell-offs it fell 28% in the 2020 crash and 82% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 47% below its DCF fair value of $142, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 79%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $88.73 to $232 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Multiples send mixed signals against Consumer Cyclical peers: cheaper on P/FCF 10.3 vs 16.5, richer on P/E 29.2 vs 19.3 and EV/EBITDA 16.1 vs 11.2 (sector median).
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 9.7% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 28 covering analysts target $148 on average, 96% above the price.
The price implies 1.3% annual cash-flow growth, 23pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 41% clears the cost of capital of 11.5% by 29pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.10).
It runs a 39% gross margin and converts 20% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is mixed: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 3.18x, but high accruals (-11.7% of assets).
ROE of 13% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.3x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 45pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 5.0% of revenue on R&D and 2.7% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $6.4B.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 22.6% over 3 years and 39.3% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 53%).
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 30.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 83.0% a year over five years.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.4x, 2.2% of sales), a maintenance pace.
own: Insiders own 26.5%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 70%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (73 sales, net $4.8M sold).
people: With about 102,700 employees, each generates about $223K of revenue, 0.6x the Consumer Cyclical median, and productivity has risen 65.2% a year.
That works out to $44K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
